MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT -- SUMMARY EXTRACT

This Master Services Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into between Solstice Freight Logistics LLC ("Carrier") and Bramwell & Ives Retail Group ("Client"), effective as of the last signature date below. This extract summarizes the operative sections of the Agreement for internal reference by both parties' accounting and operations teams.

1. Scope of Services. Carrier shall provide ground freight transportation services for Client's retail goods between Client's regional distribution centers and its store locations within the continental service area, as detailed in Schedule A. Services include standard palletized freight, temperature-controlled transport for Schedule B items, and white-glove delivery for oversized fixtures upon separate written request. Carrier will provide its own vehicles, drivers, and standard handling equipment; Client is responsible for providing accurate manifests and ensuring goods are properly packaged for transit prior to pickup.

2. Term. This Agreement begins on the effective date and continues for an initial term of twenty-four (24) months, automatically renewing for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party provides ninety (90) days' written notice of non-renewal prior to the end of the then-current term.

3. Rates and Payment Terms. Client shall pay Carrier's standard per-mile and per-pallet rates as set forth in Schedule C, invoiced monthly in arrears. Invoices are due within thirty (30) days of receipt. Late payments accrue interest at 1% per month on the unpaid balance. Rate adjustments require sixty (60) days' written notice and are capped at 5% per twelve-month period absent mutual written agreement otherwise.

4. Liability for Loss or Damage. Carrier shall be liable for loss or damage to Client's goods while in Carrier's custody, up to a maximum of $500 per shipment, unless the shipment was declared at a higher value in writing prior to pickup and an excess-value fee was paid at the time of booking. For any single shipment where Client's claimed damage exceeds $500 and no excess-value declaration was filed for that shipment, Client shall bear the cost of the amount exceeding $500; Carrier remains responsible only for the first $500 of such a claim. For shipments where an excess-value declaration was filed and the corresponding fee was paid, Carrier is liable for the full declared value of the damaged or lost goods, not merely the $500 default cap. Claims must be submitted within fourteen (14) days of delivery or, for non-delivery, within thirty (30) days of the scheduled delivery date.

5. Insurance. Carrier shall maintain commercial general liability insurance of not less than $2,000,000 per occurrence and cargo insurance of not less than $250,000 per vehicle, and shall provide certificates of insurance to Client upon request. Nothing in this section shall be construed to increase Carrier's liability under Section 4 beyond the caps stated therein.

6. Confidentiality. Each party agrees to keep confidential any pricing, manifests, customer lists, or operational data disclosed by the other party, and to use such information solely for purposes of performing under this Agreement. This obligation survives termination for a period of three (3) years.

7. Termination. Either party may terminate this Agreement for material breach upon thirty (30) days' written notice if the breach is not cured within that period. Client may additionally terminate immediately, without cure period, if Carrier's on-time delivery rate falls below 85% for two consecutive calendar months, as measured by Carrier's own tracking reports.

8. Notices. All notices under this Agreement must be sent in writing to the addresses listed in Schedule D, by certified mail or recognized courier, and are deemed received three (3) business days after mailing.

Appendix Note (Sept 21): Shipment #7788 (picked up Sept 12, delivered Sept 13) contained store fixtures valued at $2,100. The shipment arrived with visible crush damage to two fixtures. Client's records confirm no excess-value declaration was on file for Shipment #7788 at the time of booking. Client submitted a damage claim on Sept 20.
